knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)

library(dplyr)

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Morcos_2023b_copanlisib"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description: ", ui$description, "\n", sep = "")
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.13523> (open access)
* Adult backbone: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13000>, packaged as
  `Morcos_2023_copanlisib` (see the [Copanlisib (Morcos 2023)](Morcos_2023_copanlisib.html)
  article)

Copanlisib is an intravenous pan-class-I PI3K inhibitor. Morcos 2023 (Clin
Transl Sci) supported the starting dose of 28 mg/m^2 for a pediatric phase I
study (Bayer study 19176) with two models:

1. An adult whole-body PBPK model built in PK-Sim (Open Systems Pharmacology
   Suite 6.0), extended to children through PK-Sim's built-in age-dependent
   physiology. It is **not** packaged; see
   [Assumptions and deviations](#assumptions-and-deviations).
2. The adult population PK model, adapted to children by scaling every
   clearance and volume by body surface area: `P = P_adult * (BSA / 1.88)^1`.
   The adapted model was **not re-estimated**. It was used as is to estimate
   individual exposure from the pediatric samples and to simulate a virtual
   pediatric population. This is the packaged model.

The adult model cited by the pediatric paper (its reference 9, a 2022 AACR
poster) is the analysis published in full as Morcos 2023 CPT:PSP. That paper's
figures are credited as "previously presented in a poster at the Third AACR
International Meeting ... June 23-26, 2022", which is the poster the pediatric
paper cites. Every typical value, covariate effect, IIV and residual magnitude
therefore comes from Morcos 2023 CPT:PSP Table 2. The pediatric paper adds only
the BSA term.

# Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
pop <- ui$population
tibble::tibble(
  Field = names(pop),
  Value = vapply(pop, function(x) paste(as.character(x), collapse = "; "), character(1))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Population metadata carried by the model file (Morcos 2023 CTS, Methods and Results 'PopPK modeling').")
```

Thirty-one children and adolescents with relapsed or refractory solid tumors or
lymphoma were enrolled in the Rolling-6 dose escalation. Twenty-four received
28 mg/m^2 and seven received 35 mg/m^2 on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle.
After removing 30 pre-dose BLQ samples and one implausible sample, 160
concentrations from 30 patients remained. Their median age was 13 years (range
4-21) and median BSA 1.37 m^2 (range 0.64-2.44). The paper does not report the
cohort's sex split, hepatic function or enrollment region.

# Source trace

| BSA power scaling on CL, V1, Q2, V2, Q3, V3, centred on 1.88 m^2 | n/a | Morcos 2023 CTS Methods, "Population PK modeling" |

# The adaptation reduces exactly to the adult model at 1.88 m^2

With BSA = 1.88 m^2, every scaling factor is 1, so the packaged pediatric model
must reproduce the packaged adult model exactly. At any other BSA, CL and V1
must scale by exactly `BSA / 1.88`. Both are deterministic identities (the same
parameters on both sides, typical values only), so they are asserted tightly.

```{r identities}
mod      <- readModelDb("Morcos_2023b_copanlisib")
mod_typ  <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
adult_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb("Morcos_2023_copanlisib"))

cov_zero <- c(CONMED_RIFAMPICIN = 0, CONMED_ITRACONAZOLE = 0, STUDY_CHRONOS3 = 0,
              HEPIMP = 0, REGION_JAPAN = 0)

# Two subjects (male, female); 60 mg over 1 h into `central`, observations on
# the ODE state.
probe_ev <- bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(id = 1:2, time = 0, amt = 60, rate = 60, evid = 1L),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = 1:2, time = c(0.5, 1, 2, 24, 168)) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, evid = 0L)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central", SEXF = id - 1) |>
  bind_cols(tibble::as_tibble(as.list(cov_zero))) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_adult <- rxode2::rxSolve(adult_typ, events = probe_ev) |> as.data.frame()
sim_ref   <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = mutate(probe_ev, BSA = 1.88)) |> as.data.frame()
sim_small <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = mutate(probe_ev, BSA = 0.94)) |> as.data.frame()

identity_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  Check = c("Cc, pediatric model at 1.88 m^2 vs adult model (max rel. diff)",
            "CL ratio at 0.94 m^2 vs 1.88 m^2 (expected 0.5)",
            "V1 ratio at 0.94 m^2 vs 1.88 m^2 (expected 0.5)"),
  Value = c(max(abs(sim_ref$Cc / sim_adult$Cc - 1)),
            unique(round(sim_small$cl / sim_ref$cl, 12)),
            unique(round(sim_small$vc / sim_ref$vc, 12)))
)
knitr::kable(identity_tbl, digits = 12)

stopifnot(
  max(abs(sim_ref$Cc / sim_adult$Cc - 1)) < 1e-8,
  isTRUE(all.equal(sim_small$cl / sim_ref$cl, rep(0.5, nrow(sim_ref)))),
  isTRUE(all.equal(sim_small$vc / sim_ref$vc, rep(0.5, nrow(sim_ref))))
)
```

Because every clearance and volume scales with the same power of BSA, the rate
constants (`CL/V1`, `Q2/V1`, `Q2/V2`, ...) do not depend on BSA at all. With a
dose in mg/m^2, the amount given and every volume scale together, so the
**typical concentration-time profile does not depend on BSA**. That is the
mechanism behind the paper's finding of "uniform copanlisib exposures across
the investigated pediatric age range". It also means the BSA distribution of
the virtual cohort below cannot move the exposure distribution; only sex and
the random effects can.

```{r bsa-invariance}
bsa_grid <- c(0.64, 1.00, 1.37, 1.88, 2.44)
inv_ev <- tidyr::expand_grid(BSA = bsa_grid, time = c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 24, 168)) |>
  mutate(id = match(BSA, bsa_grid))
inv_ev <- bind_rows(
  inv_ev |> distinct(id, BSA) |>
    mutate(time = 0, amt = 28 * BSA, rate = 28 * BSA, evid = 1L),
  inv_ev |> mutate(amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, evid = 0L)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central", SEXF = 0) |>
  bind_cols(tibble::as_tibble(as.list(cov_zero))) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_inv <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = inv_ev) |> as.data.frame()
inv_spread <- sim_inv |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(rel_spread = (max(Cc) - min(Cc)) / mean(Cc), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(inv_spread, digits = 12,
             caption = "Relative spread of typical Cc across BSA 0.64-2.44 m^2 at 28 mg/m^2 (male reference patient).")

# Same parameters on every row: only numerical error separates the profiles.
stopifnot(max(inv_spread$rel_spread) < 1e-6)
```

# Virtual cohort

Morcos 2023 CTS Figure 5 simulates 500 virtual patients per year of age from 4
to 21 years (250 male, 250 female) with BSA sampled from NHANES III, given
28 mg/m^2 on days 1, 8 and 15. NHANES III is not distributed with this package,
so BSA for age comes from CDC 50th-percentile weight and stature (averaged
across sexes) with lognormal scatter, via the Mosteller formula. As shown above,
the choice cannot change the AUC distribution. To keep the article fast, the
cohort has 10 patients per year of age (5 male, 5 female), 180 in all.

The adult comparator is CHRONOS-1 (study 16349 part B, the monotherapy pivotal
study, 60 mg flat). Its demographics come from the `Study 16349 (Part B)` row of
Morcos 2023 CPT:PSP Table 1: 122 patients, 48.4% female, 9.0% with mild hepatic
impairment. Adults are simulated at BSA = 1.88 m^2, where the adapted model is
the adult model.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20231197)
set.seed(20231197)

growth <- tibble::tribble(
  ~age,  ~wt,  ~ht,
  4.00,  16.3, 102,
  5.00,  18.3, 109,
  6.00,  20.6, 115,
  7.00,  23.0, 121,
  8.00,  25.6, 127,
  10.00, 32.0, 138,
  12.00, 40.5, 149,
  14.00, 50.0, 162,
  16.00, 58.0, 168,
  18.00, 63.0, 170,
  21.00, 68.0, 171
)

n_per_age <- 10L
peds <- tidyr::expand_grid(AGE = 4:21, k = seq_len(n_per_age)) |>
  mutate(
    SEXF   = as.numeric(k > n_per_age / 2),
    wt_med = stats::approx(growth$age, growth$wt, xout = AGE)$y,
    ht_med = stats::approx(growth$age, growth$ht, xout = AGE)$y,
    WT     = wt_med * exp(stats::rnorm(n(), 0, 0.20)),
    HT     = ht_med * exp(stats::rnorm(n(), 0, 0.045)),
    BSA    = sqrt(HT * WT / 3600),
    dose   = 28 * BSA,
    HEPIMP = 0,
    arm    = "Pediatric 28 mg/m2"
  )

n_adult <- 200L
adults <- tibble::tibble(
  AGE    = NA_real_,
  SEXF   = as.numeric(stats::runif(n_adult) < 0.484),
  HEPIMP = as.numeric(stats::runif(n_adult) < 0.090),
  BSA    = 1.88,
  dose   = 60,
  arm    = "Adult CHRONOS-1 60 mg"
)

cohort <- bind_rows(peds, adults) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()), CONMED_RIFAMPICIN = 0, CONMED_ITRACONAZOLE = 0,
         STUDY_CHRONOS3 = 0, REGION_JAPAN = 0) |>
  select(id, arm, AGE, SEXF, HEPIMP, BSA, dose, CONMED_RIFAMPICIN,
         CONMED_ITRACONAZOLE, STUDY_CHRONOS3, REGION_JAPAN)

cohort |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    `Female (%)` = 100 * mean(SEXF),
    `BSA median (range), m^2` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", median(BSA), min(BSA), max(BSA)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Virtual cohort.")
```

# Simulation

Three 1-h infusions one week apart (days 1, 8 and 15). AUC(0-168)nd, the
exposure metric of both papers, is the AUC over the week after the third
nominal dose, i.e. from 336 to 504 h.

```{r simulate}
auc_start <- 336
auc_end   <- 504
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(0, auc_start + c(0, seq(0.25, 4, by = 0.25),
                                            seq(5, 24, by = 1),
                                            seq(28, 168, by = 4)))))

dose_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(cohort, time = c(0, 168, 336)) |>
  mutate(amt = dose, rate = dose, evid = 1L)
obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(cohort, time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, evid = 0L)
events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("arm", "AGE")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, arm)

# The observation grid already contains time 0 (pre-dose, 0 mg/L) for every
# subject; assert it rather than re-adding it.
stopifnot(all(tapply(sim_nca$time == 0, sim_nca$id, any)))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(as.data.frame(sim_nca), Cc ~ time | arm + id,
                             concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  as.data.frame(filter(events, evid == 1L) |> select(id, time, amt, arm)),
  amt ~ time | arm + id, doseu = "mg"
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = auc_start, end = auc_end,
                        cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

auc_ind <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, arm, auclast = PPORRES) |>
  mutate(auc_ug = 1000 * auclast) |>
  left_join(distinct(cohort, id, AGE), by = "id")
```

## Comparison against published exposure

Morcos 2023 CTS reports these exposures only graphically. The values below were
digitised by the maintainers from Figure 5: the pediatric simulated median
(about 2600 ug*h/L) and 90% prediction interval (about 1450-4500 ug*h/L), and
the CHRONOS-1 observed median (about 2870 ug*h/L) and 5th-95th percentiles
(about 2100-4550 ug*h/L).

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tibble(
  arm     = c("Pediatric 28 mg/m2", "Adult CHRONOS-1 60 mg"),
  auclast = c(2.600, 2.870)   # ug*h/L digitised from Figure 5, in mg*h/L
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated     = nca_res,
  reference     = published,
  by            = "arm",
  params        = "auclast",
  units         = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated median AUC(0-168)nd vs. Morcos 2023 CTS Figure 5 (digitised). * differs from reference by >20%.")

auc_summary <- auc_ind |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(auc_ug, 0.05), Q50 = median(auc_ug), Q95 = quantile(auc_ug, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(auc_summary, digits = 0,
             caption = "Simulated AUC(0-168)nd percentiles (ug*h/L).")

ped <- auc_summary[auc_summary$arm == "Pediatric 28 mg/m2", ]
adu <- auc_summary[auc_summary$arm == "Adult CHRONOS-1 60 mg", ]

stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed clearance, sex effect or BSA centring value
  # moves the whole pediatric distribution by tens of percent.
  abs(ped$Q50 / 2600 - 1) < 0.10,
  # The adult comparator: CHRONOS-1 is printed as empirical-Bayes estimates,
  # which shrink towards the mean, so only the centre is compared.
  abs(adu$Q50 / 2870 - 1) < 0.15,
  # Envelope: the 90% interval spans a factor of about 3.1 in Figure 5
  # (4500 / 1450); this checks the IIV on CL is in the right range.
  (ped$Q95 / ped$Q05) > 2, (ped$Q95 / ped$Q05) < 4.5
)
```

The simulated pediatric distribution matches Figure 5. The paper attributes the
lower pediatric median to the dose: 28 mg/m^2 is 80% of the adult 60 mg dose
adjusted for BSA. For typical patients of the same sex, the pediatric-to-adult
AUC ratio is `28 * 1.88 / 60` =
`r sprintf("%.3f", 28 * 1.88 / 60)`, whatever the child's BSA. The paper also
gives a geometric mean ratio of 101% for the *model-predicted individual* AUC of
the enrolled pediatric patients against CHRONOS-1. Those are empirical-Bayes
estimates from the 30 real patients and cannot be reproduced without their
data; they suggest the enrolled children had somewhat lower clearance than the
typical value.

```{r gmr}
gmr <- exp(mean(log(auc_ind$auc_ug[auc_ind$arm == "Pediatric 28 mg/m2"]))) /
  exp(mean(log(auc_ind$auc_ug[auc_ind$arm == "Adult CHRONOS-1 60 mg"])))
knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Simulated pediatric / adult geometric mean AUC ratio",
               "Typical-value ratio 28 * 1.88 / 60",
               "Figure 5 simulated pediatric median / CHRONOS-1 observed median (digitised)",
               "Paper: enrolled pediatric (individual estimates) vs CHRONOS-1 GMR"),
  Value = c(gmr, 28 * 1.88 / 60, 2600 / 2870, 1.01)
), digits = 3)
```

## Replicates Figure 5 of Morcos 2023 CTS

```{r figure5, fig.height = 4.5}
ped_band <- auc_ind |>
  filter(arm == "Pediatric 28 mg/m2") |>
  summarise(Q05 = quantile(auc_ug, 0.05), Q50 = median(auc_ug),
            Q95 = quantile(auc_ug, 0.95))

auc_ind |>
  filter(arm == "Pediatric 28 mg/m2") |>
  ggplot(aes(AGE, auc_ug)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 3.5, xmax = 21.5, ymin = ped_band$Q05, ymax = ped_band$Q95,
           fill = "pink", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ped_band$Q50, colour = "red") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, shape = 1, colour = "darkred") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 9000)) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "AUC(0-168)nd (ug*h/L)",
       title = "Simulated AUC(0-168)nd after three weekly doses of 28 mg/m^2",
       caption = "Median (line) and 90% prediction interval (band). Replicates the left panel of Figure 5 of Morcos 2023 CTS.") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r age-flatness}
# Figure 5: exposure is flat across age. Medians by age band, robust to which
# subjects land in the tails.
age_bands <- auc_ind |>
  filter(arm == "Pediatric 28 mg/m2") |>
  mutate(band = cut(AGE, c(3, 8, 13, 17, 21), labels = c("4-8", "9-13", "14-17", "18-21"))) |>
  group_by(band) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median_auc = median(auc_ug), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(age_bands, digits = 0, caption = "Median simulated AUC(0-168)nd by age band (ug*h/L).")
stopifnot(max(abs(age_bands$median_auc / ped_band$Q50 - 1)) < 0.25)
```

## Concentration-time profile after the third dose

```{r profile}
sim |>
  filter(time >= auc_start) |>
  mutate(tad = time - auc_start) |>
  filter(tad > 0) |>
  group_by(arm, tad) |>
  summarise(Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, 1000 * Q50, colour = arm, fill = arm)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 1000 * Q05, ymax = 1000 * Q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 168, by = 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time after third dose (h)", y = "Copanlisib (ug/L)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **The PBPK model is not packaged.** The adult and pediatric PBPK models were
  built in PK-Sim. The paper prints only the drug-specific inputs (Table 1:
  physicochemistry, a hypothetical binding partner, P-gp and CYP3A4 kinetics).
  The organ volumes, blood flows, partition coefficients, expression profiles
  and ontogeny functions are outputs of the PK-Sim database and are not
  published, so the model cannot be reconstructed from the paper.
* **The adult backbone comes from a second paper.** The pediatric paper prints
  no adult parameter values. It cites a 2022 AACR poster, and Morcos 2023
  CPT:PSP reproduces that poster's figures. All values here are from Morcos
  2023 CPT:PSP Table 2.
* **All adult covariates are kept.** The paper states the adult model was used
  "without further modification", so the sex, hepatic-impairment, Japan,
  CHRONOS-3 and comedication effects remain. For the pediatric study the DDI,
  CHRONOS-3 and Japan indicators are 0. The paper does not report the cohort's
  sex split, hepatic function or region, so the virtual cohort is half female
  (as in Figure 5) with normal hepatic function.
* **Residual error.** The pediatric study is a phase I study, so its samples
  beyond the first 20 min of an infusion use the phase I/II residual stratum
  (`STUDY_CHRONOS3 = 0`).
* **BSA source.** Figure 5 sampled BSA from NHANES III, which is not available
  here. CDC growth medians with lognormal scatter and the Mosteller formula
  are used instead. The paper does not say which BSA formula it used. Under
  BSA^1 scaling with mg/m^2 dosing, the BSA values cannot affect the simulated
  AUC (shown above).
* **Adult comparator.** CHRONOS-1 is simulated at BSA = 1.88 m^2, where the
  adapted model equals the adult model, with 48.4% female and 9.0% mild hepatic
  impairment (Morcos 2023 CPT:PSP Table 1, study 16349 part B). The Japan
  column of that row reads as 0 Japanese patients and is set to 0. Figure 5
  plots the CHRONOS-1 values as individual model-predicted (empirical-Bayes)
  exposures, which are shrunk towards the mean. The simulated adult tails are
  therefore wider than the published 5th-95th percentiles, and only the medians
  are compared.
* **Figure values are digitised.** The Figure 5 medians and intervals were read
  off the published figure by the maintainers and are accurate to about
  +/-100 ug*h/L.
* **Cohort size.** 10 virtual patients per year of age (180 in all) instead of
  500, to keep the article fast.
